ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Dwight D. Eisenhower

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for a nosebleed on dual antiplatelet therapy

text.paragraph: Nosebleed this morning that took about 25 minutes to stop. [S]

Mr. Eisenhower is a 65-year-old man about six and a half months after an anterior myocardial infarction treated with a drug-eluting stent, on aspirin 81 mg and ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily, who asked for a same-day visit. This morning, after blowing his nose, his right nostril began to bleed. He leaned forward and pinched his nose, but it took about 25 minutes to stop, and he soaked several handkerchiefs. Three days ago he had a brief bleed from the same side that stopped within five minutes. The office heating has been running high and his nose has felt dry and crusted for a week. He has had no bleeding from the gums, easy bruising, black stools, or blood in the urine, and no lightheadedness. He takes no ibuprofen or other NSAIDs and no supplements. He took his morning aspirin and ticagrelor and asks whether he should stop them. [S]

list.item:
Anterior epistaxis, right side (R04.0). A bleed from a visible vessel in Kiesselbach's area, made more likely by dry air and made longer by dual antiplatelet therapy. There is no sign of a posterior bleed, the hemoglobin is 14.3 g/dL against 14.6 g/dL in January, and the platelet count is normal. [S]
After topical anesthetic and oxymetazoline, the visible vessel on the right was cauterized with silver nitrate; the left side was not treated.
Petroleum jelly to the inside of the right nostril twice daily and saline nasal spray several times a day for two weeks; a humidifier in the office.
No nose blowing, heavy lifting, or straining for one week.
If it bleeds again: lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for 15 minutes by the clock. Go to the emergency department if bleeding lasts more than 20 minutes despite pressure, runs down the throat, or causes lightheadedness.

Myocardial infarction with a drug-eluting stent, about six and a half months ago (I25.2). Stopping antiplatelet therapy within the first year after a stent carries a risk of stent thrombosis that outweighs the risk of a controllable anterior nosebleed. [S]
Continue aspirin 81 mg and ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily without interruption.
Avoid NSAIDs; use acetaminophen for pain.

Essential hypertension (I10). Blood pressure 146/86 mmHg today, raised by anxiety about the bleeding; it was 124/76 mmHg in March. [S]
No change; recheck at the review next month and send two weeks of home readings.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes (2025); Clinical Practice Guideline: Nosebleed (Epistaxis) (2020)

Follow-up: Coronary disease review next month as planned. Return the same day or go to the emergency department for a nosebleed that does not stop with 20 minutes of pressure. Next scheduled visit 2026-05-11: seven-month coronary disease review after return to full-time work. [S]
